hints: Treat every connection as an unweighted edge and start BFS at computer 1.
Store the parent of each computer when first discovered.
BFS layers are route lengths in edges; reconstruct from n or print IMPOSSIBLE.
analogy: Search outward from computer 1 one connection-count layer at a time.
example: If route 1-4-5 exists, it uses three computers; the route string is reconstructed by following parents from 5 back to 1.
algorithm: Run BFS on the undirected graph from 1; if n is reached, follow parent pointers to 1, reverse the list, and print its size and vertices.
correctness: BFS visits vertices in nondecreasing edge distance, so the first parent chain to n has minimum connections and therefore minimum computers.
